Key results

bcftools.no.chr6.R000648

  • Model 1 (ROH + age + sex + PC1–5 + APOE ε4): ROH OR 1.19 (95% CI 0.68–2.07; P = 0.54), N = 2,226 (23 carrier cases / 31 carrier controls). Without APOE (original M1 specification) ROH OR 1.12 (95% CI 0.65–1.94; P = 0.68).
  • APOE ε4 (per allele) in Model 1: OR 1.44 (95% CI 1.21–1.72; P = 4.0e-05).
  • Model 2 ROH × APOE ε4 interaction: ratio of ORs 0.82 (95% CI 0.23–2.90; P = 0.74).
  • Accounting for kinship (GLMM, kinship variance τ = 0.22): ROH OR 1.19 (95% CI 0.67–2.12; P = 0.55); unrelated subset (N = 1,570, 37 carriers): ROH OR 1.29 (95% CI 0.66–2.52; P = 0.46).
  • Primary ancestry EUR (auto: highest mean global ancestry, 0.58): local EUR at ROH locus (per haplotype, given global): OR 0.96 (95% CI 0.84–1.09; P = 0.49); EUR-origin ROH haplotype vs other origins: OR 0.25 (95% CI 0.05–1.21; P = 0.053).
  • Smallest ancestry-related P values (exploratory; see tables for all): ROH haplotype of EUR origin vs other origins: OR 0.25 (P = 0.053); APOE ε4 × global AFR: OR 0.89 (P = 0.057); ROH × local EUR: OR 0.52 (P = 0.070); global NAM (per 10%): OR 0.73 (P = 0.15).

P values are nominal (unadjusted); no multiple-testing correction is applied because the number of individuals and ROH regions gives no power after correction. Interpret associations as exploratory and look for replication across cohorts. Case-control data show association with AD status; they cannot establish effects on progression.

Figures

Should global ancestry be included with local ancestry?

Decision: yes — every primary local-ancestry model also contains global ancestry of the same component (plus PC1–5); the PC-only version is kept as a labelled sensitivity analysis.

Local ancestry at a locus is a draw around an individual's genome-wide (global) ancestry. Without global ancestry, a local-ancestry coefficient mixes the locus-specific signal with every genome-wide correlate of ancestry (polygenic background, socio-environmental exposures, recruitment). Conditioning on global ancestry is the standard admixture-mapping contrast and isolates what is specific to this locus. The cost is collinearity, quantified below: the variance inflation of local ancestry is at most 1.21, which is modest when VIF < 5. Global ancestry is entered one component at a time (or K−1 components with a reference) because the proportions sum to one. Because ROH carriers are homozygous for one ancestry, the ancestral origin of the ROH haplotype (Fig. 3c) is the most direct test of which ancestry's ROH drives an association.

Relatedness (kinship)

Source: KING table /tmp/synthetic/cohort.kin0. Primary family: Firth (no random effect).

Kinship is a property of pairs, so it is not entered as an ordinary covariate. It is handled as (i) a GRM random effect (logistic mixed model), (ii) family-cluster-robust standard errors and (iii) a maximal unrelated subset. The individual-level relatedness quantity that is a covariate, the inbreeding coefficient (genome-wide F_ROH, focal region excluded), is added in K7/K8. Relatives who share the same IBD segment are not independent observations: if ROH carriers cluster in families, models that ignore kinship give P values that are too small. Compare the rows below; if they agree, relatedness does not drive the result.

Methods (draft text)

Association between carrier status of each retained high-confidence ROH region and AD was estimated with Firth bias-reduced logistic regression (penalized likelihood with Jeffreys prior) to accommodate the small number of carriers. P values are penalized likelihood-ratio tests in which the tested coefficients are fixed at zero while the full-design penalty is retained; confidence intervals are Wald intervals. The primary model (Model 1) adjusted for age (centred, per decade), sex, the first five genetic principal components and APOE ε4 dosage (0/1/2); Model 2 added a ROH × ε4-dosage product term. Age, sex and principal components were adjustment covariates only and were never modelled as effect modifiers. Global ancestry proportions (per 10%) and local ancestry at the ROH locus (number of haplotypes, 0–2) were analysed as covariates and as effect modifiers; local-ancestry models were adjusted for global ancestry of the same component, with principal-component-only models as sensitivity analyses. Because ROH carriers are homozygous for a single ancestry at the locus, we additionally contrasted carriers by the ancestral origin of the homozygous haplotype. Ancestry-specific APOE effects were assessed with APOE × global ancestry terms and APOE × local ancestry at APOE. Relatedness was addressed with a logistic mixed model including a genetic relationship matrix random effect (penalized quasi-likelihood with REML variance estimation and score tests), family-cluster-robust standard errors, a maximal unrelated subset, and adjustment for genome-wide autozygosity (FROH, excluding the tested region). Covariate-standardized risks were obtained by g-computation. All tests were two-sided; the model catalog was fixed before fitting; models lacking support (fewer than 3 carriers or non-carriers, or fewer than 5 carriers per modifier level for interactions) are reported as not estimable. P values are nominal; no multiple-testing correction was applied because the number of individuals and ROH regions gives no power after correction, so associations are exploratory and were assessed for replication across cohorts.

Limitations

  • One retained region with few carriers: interaction and origin-specific estimates have wide intervals; non-estimable cells are reported, not dropped.
  • The GLMM uses PQL, which can underestimate the kinship variance for binary traits; its score tests are the GMMAT/SAIGE standard but are asymptotic.
  • Wald intervals and asymptotic LR P values are approximate with sparse cells.
  • P values are nominal (no multiple-testing correction); with many tests some nominal associations are expected by chance, so replication across cohorts is required.
  • Associations from case-control status; no inference about disease progression or causality.

tables/all_association_tests.tsv (every test), tables/all_coefficients.tsv (every term, natural units), tables/effect_contrasts.tsv, tables/predicted_risk.tsv, tables/ancestry_collinearity.tsv, analysis_manifest.json (catalog fixed before fitting), apoe_audit.json, figures/ (PDF, SVG, 600-dpi PNG/TIFF).
